stories.headline: Colorado voters approve Amendment 87, restoring graduated income tax for top earners
stories.summary:
Colorado voters this week approved Amendment 87, a roughly $2 billion annual tax increase on the highest-earning households and corporations. The Associated Press called the race at 10:49 a.m. Friday, with the measure leading 51.4% to 48.6%. It brings a graduated income tax back to Colorado for the first time since 1986, replacing the flat rate required by the state constitution.

The measure creates six new brackets that raise taxes on households and businesses making more than about $500,000 while cutting taxes on the first $100,000 of income. A household with $75,000 in taxable income will pay $275 less per year, a family earning $550,000 will pay $1,175 more, and someone earning $10 million will owe an additional $376,000.

The revenue can be spent on health care, public schools and child care. As a result, the Joint Budget Committee will return to work next week on a spending plan that does not require the $1.6 billion in cuts state analysts had feared. Together with Proposition NN, the measure marks a shift in Colorado's approach to funding public services beyond TABOR limits.

stories.headline: House Democrats elect Rep. Jennifer Bacon of Denver as next Speaker
stories.summary:
Colorado House Democrats on Friday elected Rep. Jennifer Bacon of Denver as their next speaker, choosing her over Speaker Pro Tempore Andrew Boesenecker of Fort Collins. Bacon, a leader of the caucus's progressive wing, will become the first Black woman elected speaker and the sixth woman to hold the post. Vote percentages were kept confidential.

The vote followed Tuesday's elections, in which Democrats secured a record 49 of the chamber's 65 seats. Newly elected members from Colorado Springs and Erie received long ovations, including Rep.-elect Jeff Livingston, the first Democrat to represent House District 15.

Boesenecker had pitched his candidacy on collective bargaining rights, lowering costs, public education, health care and holding Big Tech accountable. Bacon said she is not afraid to lead a 49-member caucus and told members her role would be to lift them and their communities up. Current Speaker Julie McCluskie of Dillon administered the roll call.

stories.headline: Colorado Democrats secure first supermajorities in both legislative chambers
stories.summary:
Colorado Democrats on Friday secured supermajorities in both the state House and Senate, which lawmakers say is a first in state history. Democrats flipped four legislative seats, exceeding their projections, even though Republicans outspent them on legislative races.

The supermajorities allow Democrats to override vetoes from incoming Gov.-elect Phil Weiser and to refer constitutional amendments to the ballot without Republican votes. That could weaken Weiser's influence over the General Assembly and force Democrats to confront policy questions they have avoided by relying on the threat of vetoes from Gov. Jared Polis.

Senate Democrats chose Sen. Dylan Roberts of Frisco as majority leader on Thursday, and he vowed to repair the rift between progressives and moderates. House Minority Leader Jarvis Caldwell of Colorado Springs said his party's candidates ran on affordability and crime and that he wants to understand what drove voters toward Democrats. Among the decisive races, Democrat Aaron Gutierrez won Senate District 3 in Pueblo.

stories.headline: Boebert campaign alleges 'unusual voting patterns' while trailing Laubacher
stories.summary:
A lawyer for Rep. Lauren Boebert's campaign said he is investigating what he called very unusual voting patterns as the Republican trails Democrat Eileen Laubacher in the 4th Congressional District. As of 6 p.m. Friday, Laubacher led by 3,172 votes, or 0.83 percentage points, with more than 97% of the vote tallied. The Associated Press had not called the race.

Laubacher, a retired Navy rear admiral and former National Security Council official, led by more than 7,000 votes on election night, but her margin narrowed as later ballots were counted. That is typical in Colorado, where Republicans tend to vote later. Attorney Scott Gessler said the campaign expects a recount and did not specify what patterns he meant.

Colorado law triggers an automatic recount when the margin is 0.5% or less of the leading candidate's vote total, so the current margin lies outside the threshold. A Boebert fundraising email mischaracterized the law, saying the threshold applies to a margin of 0.5% or lower. Candidates may pay for a recount if the margin exceeds the automatic threshold.

stories.headline: Update: Slain Lakewood agent identified as Nicholas Graham; suspect killed in RTD bus shootout
stories.summary:
Lakewood police identified the agent killed in Thursday's shootout aboard an RTD bus as Nicholas Graham, 33, of the department's Major Crimes Unit. Graham joined the department in 2019 and was credited by Chief Philip Smith with helping solve more than 300 cases. The suspect was also killed, and officials had not released his name.

According to police, the incident began with a hit-and-run earlier Thursday. An officer recognized the suspect near Colfax Avenue and Wadsworth Boulevard at 6:29 p.m. and requested backup. The suspect fired multiple rounds at approaching officers, with the first shots-fired call coming at about 6:32 p.m. A bystander was also injured.

Two of the three wounded agents were released Friday and the third remains hospitalized; all are expected to recover. The First Judicial District Attorney's Office is investigating the officers' use of force. A memorial of flowers and cards has grown outside the Lakewood Police Department, and officers from across the metro area took part in a procession at Denver Health on Thursday night.

stories.headline: RTD Route 76 riders and union react after deadly bus shooting
stories.summary:
Regular riders of RTD's Route 76 said they were stunned after Thursday night's shooting that killed a Lakewood police agent and wounded three other agents and a passenger. Crime scene tape and flowers remained at Colfax and Wadsworth on Friday. Rider Nate Weickum said Graham had spoken with him earlier that day.

Ronald Short of ATU 1001, the union representing RTD employees, said the bus driver is physically unharmed but shaken. Short praised the operator for keeping his composure and said the union will provide support in the coming days. RTD is also offering counseling to employees who work the route.

RTD had not responded to Denver7's questions about whether additional safety measures would be added. Short said he believes the agency is handling safety appropriately and noted that RTD offers refresher training for operators, which the union is open to expanding on handling such situations.

stories.headline: Nonprofits lean on Colorado Gives Day amid rising need and federal cuts
stories.summary:
Colorado nonprofits are preparing for Colorado Gives Day on Dec. 8, with giving having begun Sunday. Organizers hope to top last year's record of $56.6 million, a 3.3% increase over the prior year, which supported more than 4,600 organizations. Nonprofits say the event is increasingly vital as federal funding cuts and state budget problems add pressure.

Food Bank of the Rockies reports food insecurity at a 12-year high, with a roughly 17% year-over-year increase in need at mobile pantry distributions. CEO Erin Pulling attributed much of it to SNAP reductions, as thousands of Coloradans lost benefits after federal work and immigration-status rules took effect.

Costs have also risen. Filling a semitruck tank now costs $1,000, up from $500, adding $63,000 a month in expenses, while higher food prices added $100,000. Homeward Alliance in Larimer County calls the day its most important fundraiser other than its annual gala.

stories.headline: Predators beat Avalanche 3-2 in overtime on Stamkos power-play goal
stories.summary:
Steven Stamkos scored a power-play goal in overtime Thursday night as the Nashville Predators beat the Colorado Avalanche 3-2 at Ball Arena. It was the Avalanche's second straight loss. Colorado is now 6-1-2 at home.

Devon Toews hit the post on a chance to win it, then was called for hooking at the other end, putting Nashville on the power play. Ross Colton, traded to Nashville by the Avalanche, opened the scoring in the first period, and Jaden Schwartz tied it at 1-1. Parker Kelly tied the game again in the second on a 2-on-1 after a pass from Logan O'Connor, who recorded his first point of the season after missing the first 11 games.

Coach Jared Bednar said he was happy with the effort and that the team defended harder and more committed than in recent losses, including a 6-2 defeat in Nashville 11 days earlier. Mackenzie Blackwood made 22 saves.

topStory.headline: Security Researchers Find White House Network Computers Acting as Residential Proxy Exit Nodes
topStory.summary:
Note: The assigned topic, a possible new White House run by Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis, is not addressed in the source material provided. The only article supplied, from SecurityWeek, concerns a cybersecurity finding, and this summary covers that reporting only.

Security firm Layer3 Intel reported that six IP addresses on AS2650, the network reserved for the Executive Office of the President, were used by 28 residential proxy services between October 5 and November 3. The firm said its residential proxy enumeration pipeline exited through the White House network 236 separate times. Such exits can be used by anyone who signs up for a public residential proxy service to route requests through them.

Layer3 Intel said most of the observed activity occurred in the evening, between 5 p.m. and midnight Eastern Time, with almost none in the early morning. The firm said that pattern suggests an individual rather than a public guest Wi-Fi network, namely someone regularly on the White House network late in the day whose device is infected with a proxy software development kit. Synthient, a startup that identifies residential proxies, VPNs and bot infrastructure, said the traffic came from Windows 11 machines running the Infatica SDK.

Infatica is a Singapore-based web-data and proxy provider that says it offers access to more than 45 million residential, mobile and datacenter IP addresses worldwide. Investigative journalist Brian Krebs has reported that Infatica's founder, Vladimir Fomenko, also owns King Servers, a hosting provider that hosted six of the eight internet addresses Russian state-sponsored hackers used in the 2016 U.S. election attacks. The source article does not allege a connection between those past events and the White House findings.

Layer3 Intel's report also said residential proxies have spread to remote locations, including Saint Helena, Ascension and Tristan da Cunha, where it recorded 413 addresses and more than 32,000 observations split between Starlink and the local provider Sure Saint Helena. Exits were also seen in Antarctica, the Chagos Islands, the Falklands, Norfolk Island, Pitcairn, South Georgia, Svalbard and Tokelau. The article did not include a response from the White House or describe any remediation steps.
